board.title: Space adventure
board.story: Die Geschichte spielt in einem 3D animiertn Weltraum. Es muss keine hyper realistische Welt sein, aber auch nicht block style. Die Geschichte Beginnt damit das ein Wurmloch aufgeht und ein Raumschiff, ein kleiner Jäger erscheint. Sobald das Wurmloch geschollen ist wechselt die Kamera in das Raumschiff und man sieht das Cocpit aus Sicht des Piloten. Mit dem Auftrag der in einem Bildschirm zu lesen ist. "Zerstöre alle sechs Ziele in diesem Sektor" In den nächsten Szenen sieht man wie das Raumschif Ziele angreift. Einige mit Laser, einige mit Torpedos. Kurz bevor das letzte Ziel zerstört wurde erscheint ein neues Wurmloch und die feindliche Flotte taucht auf. Gerade als Die Flotte unser Raumschiff angreifen will ist das letzte Zeil zerstört und das Raumschiff verlässt Die Scene durch ein neues Wurmloch.
board.message: Keine besondere Botschaft. Einfach ein spannendes Weltraumabenteuer,

comments.text: Bitte darauf achten das Die Raumschiffe nicht mit Raumschiffen aus z. B. Starktrak oder Krieg der Sterne oder so verwechselt werden können.
comments.reply: Die Entwürfe setzen auf eigene Silhouetten, Proportionen, Oberflächen und Lichtsignaturen statt auf Vorlagen bekannter Filmraumschiffe. Auch Cockpit, Wurmlöcher, Sounds und Symbole sollen eigenständig gestaltet werden. Eine Verwechslungsfreiheit lässt sich erst anhand konkreter Entwurfsbilder beurteilen; bitte diese vor der Umsetzung prüfen. Die folgenden Beschreibungen sind dafür die erste Designvorgabe.

characters.name: Needlefin pilot
characters.description: The anonymous pilot of Needlefin, shown only through a first-person cockpit perspective. No face, name or full-body appearance is established. If hands enter the frame, use understated dark flight gloves consistently; do not invent a portrait or recognizable franchise costume. The pilot acts decisively under pressure, completes the six-target mission and escapes. Use the existing cockpit composition as a perspective reference, not as a character model sheet.

characters.name: Needlefin — small mission fighter
characters.description: An original, smoothly modelled single-seat spacecraft. Compact flattened seed-shaped hull, short curved nose, one offset dorsal fin and two recessed vent-like propulsion slots integrated into the rear body. No separate engine pods or broad wings. Deep petrol-blue ceramic panels, copper seams and turquoise engine light. A narrow smoked canopy sits near the front. Slight asymmetry gives it a recognizable silhouette. Stylized cinematic 3D, neither photorealistic nor block-built. Maintain the same proportions, markings and lighting throughout. Reference sketch brief: front three-quarter view, side silhouette and rear propulsion detail on a neutral background. Develop independently rather than adapting an existing franchise design.

characters.name: Six unmanned sector relays
characters.description: Six separate hostile, unmanned orbital relay devices. Each has a rounded triangular ceramic core surrounded by three unequal curved shielding plates, with an amber light in its centre. Use the same design family with small variations in plate orientation and damage. Their centres flash white immediately before destruction, making successful hits readable on a small screen. No inhabited stations or visible casualties. The six devices must remain individually accounted for: targets 1 and 2 are destroyed in shot 3, target 3 in shot 4, target 4 in shot 5, target 5 in shot 6 and target 6 in shot 7. Reference sketch brief: one intact relay, one damaged relay and a simple layout of all six.

characters.name: The arriving hostile fleet
characters.description: An original fleet consisting of one large command vessel and four smaller escorts. Their silhouettes resemble layered, uneven river stones with deep channels between overlapping armour shells. Broad compact bodies, no exposed bridges or familiar wing arrangements. Charcoal armour, pale mineral edges and narrow vermilion light strips distinguish them immediately from the turquoise hero fighter. The command vessel has three staggered armour masses around an off-centre glowing channel. Escorts share the visual language without being identical miniatures. Reference sketch brief: fleet silhouettes at matching scale, plus a front three-quarter view of the command vessel. Avoid recognizable franchise shapes, markings and weapon effects.

settings.name: The silent relay sector
settings.description: A stylized cinematic 3D space environment with a deep indigo background, sparse stars, a soft violet dust cloud and a distant pale planet partly outside the frame. Six orbital relays occupy a loose curved corridor, allowing a readable forward attack route. A few slow-moving rock fragments provide parallax but never obscure the action. Cool environmental rim lighting contrasts with warm explosions. Compose for portrait 9:16: keep critical objects near the central vertical axis and leave the lower and right edges free of essential information for platform overlays. Reference sketch brief: a vertical establishing composition and a simple overhead route diagram.

settings.name: Needlefin cockpit
settings.description: The interior of the same hero fighter, seen from the seated pilot's eyes. A curved canopy frames the sector ahead. Two low copper-edged control surfaces surround one central, stable mission display. No visible pilot face is required; gloved hands may briefly appear at the bottom of the frame. English mission text must be large and clearly readable: "DESTROY ALL SIX TARGETS IN THIS SECTOR". A simple six-light progress indicator supports continuity without requiring additional explanatory captions. No fictional brand logos or familiar franchise interface layouts. Reference sketch brief: portrait pilot-eye composition with the mission display inside the central safe area.

settings.name: Fold-space apertures
settings.description: Temporary spatial openings, not permanent physical gates. A thin irregular luminous seam splits open into an elongated oval with rippling layers and a dark displaced star field at its centre. Distortion should remain localized so the ship stays readable. The hero's arrival and escape apertures glow turquoise-white; the fleet's larger aperture glows violet with a warm red inner edge. Each opening visibly expands, stabilizes, then contracts after passage. Reference sketch brief: opening, stable passage and closing silhouettes against the same star field. Avoid imitating a recognizable portal effect from an existing production.

shots.title: Space tears open
shots.action: Start immediately with a luminous seam ripping open in the centre of the portrait frame. An elongated turquoise-white wormhole expands and the small fighter bursts through, close enough to establish its distinctive shape. Its thrusters flare as it banks into the relay sector. The aperture contracts and closes completely before the cockpit cut. Sketch brief: a small fighter emerging diagonally toward the viewer, framed by a tall glowing aperture; distant relay lights hint at the route ahead.
shots.camera: Exterior front three-quarter view. Begin close to the opening, then make a short controlled pullback as the fighter passes. Keep the entire ship readable; use background parallax rather than excessive camera shake.
shots.audio: Immediate low spatial crack followed by a sharp rising whoosh and a compact propulsion surge. The wormhole closes with a descending shimmer. An original electronic action pulse begins underneath. No speech.

shots.title: Six targets. One fighter.
shots.action: Cut into the fighter from the pilot's perspective after the arrival aperture has closed. The central display already shows "DESTROY ALL SIX TARGETS IN THIS SECTOR" in large stable English text; do not spend reading time on a typing animation. Six amber indicator lights illuminate together. Through the canopy, the first two relays line up ahead. Keep the mission readable for most of the shot. Sketch brief: a framed cockpit view with the mission screen in the middle and two distant targets visible above it.
shots.camera: Steady pilot-eye view with a slight forward drift. Keep the display close to front-facing, not severely foreshortened. Avoid a camera spin or rapid zoom while the viewer reads.
shots.audio: Brief interface activation tone and restrained cockpit hum. The action pulse gains momentum. No voiceover or spoken mission briefing.

shots.title: Targets one and two
shots.action: The fighter performs one sweeping attack pass. Two short turquoise laser bursts hit two separate relays in succession. Clearly show the first relay flash and break apart before the second impact. Debris travels away from the fighter's route, and both destroyed positions remain visibly empty. No extra devices are destroyed in the background. Sketch brief: two readable impact beats along a curved flight path, with the fighter crossing between them.
shots.camera: Exterior rear three-quarter tracking view. Follow the ship's bank while keeping both relays ahead in frame. Use a smooth continuous move rather than cutting on every laser shot.
shots.audio: Two distinct pairs of crisp laser pulses, each answered by a short stylized impact and controlled explosion. Add a lateral flyby sweep. These are cinematic designed sounds, not realistic sound propagation in a vacuum.

shots.title: A torpedo finds its mark
shots.action: A small underside launch hatch opens and releases one compact torpedo with a warm white propulsion trail. The torpedo curves toward the third relay and detonates inside its shielding plates. The target breaks into a few large, readable fragments. The fighter continues past without stopping. Sketch brief: fighter in the upper-left centre, torpedo trail drawing a curve toward a relay in the lower central area.
shots.camera: Begin close beneath the fighter at launch, then pan smoothly along the torpedo's path. End on the impact with the hero ship still visible farther behind, preserving spatial orientation.
shots.audio: Mechanical hatch click, muted launch thump and accelerating torpedo whistle, followed by one deeper impact. Give the explosion a short bass accent without covering the next musical beat.

shots.title: Through the debris
shots.action: Return to pilot-eye view. Three of the six progress lights are already extinguished. The fighter threads a generous gap between drifting fragments, lines up the fourth relay and fires a short laser burst. The relay flashes and disintegrates beyond the canopy; the fourth indicator goes dark, leaving two lit. Use a simple targeting bracket without more readable text. Sketch brief: cockpit foreground, an unobstructed target near the centre and a few fragments framing the outer edges.
shots.camera: Pilot-eye view with a restrained bank that settles before the shot is fired. Keep the horizon cues and targeting bracket stable enough for the attack to read on a phone.
shots.audio: Close cockpit hum, a passing debris hiss, short laser pulses and a filtered impact. The action pulse becomes tighter and faster in perceived intensity without making the scene visually frantic.

shots.title: One target left — company arrives
shots.action: The fighter launches a torpedo at the fifth relay; its destruction is clearly visible in the foreground. Immediately afterward, a much larger violet-red spatial seam opens behind the remaining sixth relay. The command vessel pushes through, followed by four escorts. Their scale reveals that the fighter is badly outmatched. Leave the sixth relay intact and visible. Sketch brief: a small foreground explosion, one surviving amber relay and an enormous opening revealing layered fleet silhouettes behind it.
shots.camera: Exterior side three-quarter tracking shot. After the fifth impact, widen and tilt slightly to reveal the fleet entering behind the final target. Keep the fighter in the composition as a scale reference.
shots.audio: Torpedo launch and impact, interrupted by a heavy spatial rupture. Drop the musical pulse briefly into a low ominous note as the command vessel appears. Introduce a restrained threat tone.

shots.title: Finish the mission
shots.action: The fleet turns toward the fighter. Red weapon channels brighten and targeting lights converge, visibly preparing an attack. Instead of engaging the fleet, the fighter makes one decisive pass at the final relay and fires a concentrated laser burst. The sixth target breaks apart just before the fleet can fire. Briefly cut to the cockpit display: all six progress lights are dark and a large green check symbol confirms completion. Sketch brief: the tiny fighter crossing the final amber relay while the looming command vessel's red weapon channels charge behind it.
shots.camera: Start on an exterior three-quarter view that includes fighter, final target and command vessel. Track the final attack in one readable move, then use a brief cockpit insert for the completion symbol. Do not obscure the sixth impact with the insert.
shots.audio: Rising enemy weapon-charge tone, one forceful laser burst and a sharp final target impact. A short confirmation chime cuts through the tension. The music launches into its final escape accent.

shots.title: Gone before the first shot
shots.action: A new, small turquoise-white wormhole opens directly ahead of the fighter, spatially separate from the fleet's arrival aperture. The fighter accelerates through it. The opening snaps shut just before the fleet releases its first volley; the red shots cross the empty location where the fighter had been. End with a brief readable hold on the closed escape point and the outmanoeuvred fleet. No additional targets remain intact. Sketch brief: fighter entering a narrow bright aperture, distant fleet aligned behind it, followed by an empty-space final composition.
shots.camera: Exterior chase view for the approach, then hold outside the escape aperture as the fighter disappears. Let the missed volley pass through the frame to emphasize the narrow escape. Finish with a stable composition rather than a long fade.
shots.audio: Strong engine surge, rising fold-space whoosh and a crisp closing snap. The fleet's delayed volley passes with a low sweep. End on a short satisfying musical hit with a small reverberant tail. No spoken outro.
